newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Transaero plans share issue after audit.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Transaero plans share issue after audit.

text.p: Russia's private AO Transaero airline said on Wednesday it was planning a share issue, but the size and timing were still uncertain.

A company official said in answer to an enquiry that Ernst & Young would soon complete an audit of Transaero for the first half of 1996 acccording to Western standards, and details of the share issue would be resolved after that.
Transaero has appointed ABN AMRO to manage the issue.

Earlier this year Transaero officials said the company planned to issue ordinary registered shares. They said Transaero had signed an agreement with ABN AMRO to make the Dutch bank the company's registrar from the second half of 1996.
It is not clear whether the issue will be a public offering or a private placement.
Transaero's operating profit was $27.5 million on sales of $156 million in 1995, up from $15.1 million on $65.6 million in 1994, company figures according to Russian accounting standards show.
The number of passengers last year doubled to 1.1 million, and the load factor on scheduled flights rose to 66.6 percent from 60.3 percent in 1994.
AO Transaero was established in 1991. Russia's Aeroflot International Airlines owns five per cent of Transaero.
Employees own 15 percent of shares, the rest belonging to several Russian aircraft design bureaux and other shareholders.
The company operates 14 passenger aircraft making regular flights to 27 destinations in the former Soviet Union and seven other international regular and charter routes.
